subject.title: [Bug]: Non-Anthropic models output tool calls as plain text '[tool: exec]' instead of tool_use blocks

question: Should OpenClaw treat argument-less text markers like `[tool: exec]` as retry/fallback/block signals for non-native tool providers, or leave them as provider incompatibility diagnostics?
rationale: The code can detect or warn on the marker, but deciding whether to retry, fail over, force tool use, shrink tools, or block provider use changes runtime/provider compatibility policy.

options.title: Add guarded recovery policy
options.body: Detect bare registered-tool markers as failed tool intent and recover through a maintainer-approved retry, fallback, or warning/block path without executing missing arguments.

options.title: Limit to diagnostics and docs
options.body: Keep current execution behavior, expand diagnostics for `[tool:name]`, and direct unreliable backends to `compat.supportsTools: false` or manual-only use.

options.title: Promote bare markers directly
options.body: Turn `[tool:name]` into a tool call without arguments, accepting the risk of wrong or incomplete tool execution.

recommendation.title: Add guarded recovery policy
recommendation.body: Detect bare registered-tool markers as failed tool intent and recover through a maintainer-approved retry, fallback, or warning/block path without executing missing arguments.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns adjacent diagnostics and the SDK-boundary decision that keeps plain-text promotion private, making him the best routed owner for the policy choice.
